# Finding $a$ such that $\psi_k(x) = \mathrm{Tr}_k(ax)$ for all $x \in k$

## Setting Up the Problem

In the standard framework of local/global field theory, the **standard additive character** $\psi_k$ of a field $k$ (e.g., a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ or a $p$-adic field) is defined via the field trace. Specifically:

$$\psi_k(x) \;=\; \psi_0\!\bigl(\mathrm{Tr}_{k/k_0}(x)\bigr)$$

where $k_0$ is the prime field (or base field) and $\psi_0$ is the standard additive character of $k_0$.

## Determining $a$

The condition requires:
$$\psi_0\!\bigl(\mathrm{Tr}_k(x)\bigr) \;=\; \psi_0\!\bigl(\mathrm{Tr}_k(ax)\bigr) \quad \forall\, x \in k$$

Since $\psi_0$ is injective on the appropriate range, this forces:
$$\mathrm{Tr}_k(x) = \mathrm{Tr}_k(ax) \quad \forall\, x \in k$$

Rearranging:
$$\mathrm{Tr}_k\bigl((1-a)\,x\bigr) = 0 \quad \forall\, x \in k$$

## Using Non-degeneracy of the Trace Form

The **trace bilinear form** $(x,y) \mapsto \mathrm{Tr}_k(xy)$ is **non-degenerate** on $k$. Therefore:
$$\mathrm{Tr}_k\bigl((1-a)\,x\bigr) = 0 \;\;\forall\, x \in k \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (1-a)\,x = 0 \;\;\forall\, x \in k$$

Taking $x = 1$:
$$1 - a = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a = 1$$

## Verifying $a = 1$

With $a = 1$:
$$\mathrm{Tr}_k(1 \cdot x) = \mathrm{Tr}_k(x) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \psi_k(x) = \psi_0(\mathrm{Tr}_k(x)) \;\checkmark$$

This holds identically for **every** $x \in k$ by the very definition of the standard additive character.

## Conclusion

The unique element satisfying the condition is $a = 1$, and **yes**, it is possible (in fact, it is necessary) for $a$ to equal $1$.

$$\boxed{1}$$
